experiments.hypothesis: The target audience for the product will be small to medium-sized tech companies that need efficient customer data management.
experiments.method: Create a short online survey using Google Forms and distribute it via LinkedIn groups, Twitter, and relevant Slack communities. Collect demographic data and pain points related to customer data handling.
experiments.metric: Number of survey responses and percentage of respondents who identify customer data management as a significant pain point.
experiments.go_threshold: At least 20 responses with 70% or more indicating this pain point.

experiments.hypothesis: Small tech businesses experience specific pain points when managing customer data, such as data fragmentation and lack of integration.
experiments.method: Conduct 5 in-depth phone interviews with owners or managers of small tech firms. Use a semi-structured interview guide to uncover pain points and desired features.
experiments.metric: Number of distinct pain points identified across interviews.
experiments.go_threshold: At least 3 distinct pain points consistently mentioned.

experiments.hypothesis: A cloud-based CRM solution will attract early adopters willing to sign up for a beta version.
experiments.method: Build a simple landing page using Carrd or Wix that describes the proposed solution and includes a sign-up form for beta access. Promote the page via LinkedIn posts and relevant forums.
experiments.metric: Number of sign-ups for beta access.

experiments.hypothesis: A subscription-based SaaS pricing model will be viable and competitive within the target market.
experiments.method: Perform a quick competitive analysis of 5 similar SaaS products, noting their pricing tiers and feature sets. Summarize findings in a spreadsheet.
experiments.metric: Average price point of comparable products.
experiments.go_threshold: Target price falls within the $10-$50 per month range.

experiments.hypothesis: The product can be developed while remaining compliant with GDPR requirements.
experiments.method: Review GDPR compliance requirements for SaaS products and consult a freelance legal advisor for a compliance checklist. Document any necessary data handling or privacy features.
experiments.metric: Completion of a GDPR compliance checklist with no critical gaps.
experiments.go_threshold: Checklist completed with all critical items addressed.

recommendation.rationale: The founder has not provided any substantive details about the product idea, target audience, problem, solution, business model, or constraints. All key fields are missing, and the only evidence available is the placeholder text. The risk assessment indicates a high skeptic score (10) and multiple regulatory, false‑positive, and hidden cost risks. While the founder expresses intent to develop a product and has outlined a set of experiments, none have been executed, so there is no empirical evidence to support the viability of the idea. The lack of a clear value proposition and differentiation from the status quo (planilhas) further weakens the case. Therefore, the appropriate verdict is INVESTIGATE, with a low confidence level reflecting the critical evidence gaps.
conditions: Define product idea with clear problem statement, target audience, and solution description.
Specify business model, pricing strategy, and constraints (technical, regulatory, resource).
Execute the proposed experiments to gather data on pain points, market size, and willingness to pay.
Validate GDPR compliance and other regulatory requirements before development.
Demonstrate differentiation from indirect competitors (planilhas) and identify unique value proposition.

Re‑evaluate risk score after evidence collection.
